Activity.description: A line of business carried on at an establishment.

is_primary.description: Deliberately NOT uniquely constrained. Some programmes speak of "primary industrial activity(ies)" in the plural, and an activity matching a narrative category is primary regardless of its code.

primacy_justification_text.description: Receipts ordering is stored as advisory guidance with an operator-supplied justification, never as an enforced rule.

Activity.title: Activity

AssignmentMethod.description: How a candidate code came to be proposed or set.
AssignmentMethod.title: AssignmentMethod

AttributeDefinition.description: The registry entry for a fact the system may collect or a rule may test. A rule referencing an unregistered attribute, or one at a scope that disagrees with this entry, fails CI. This is what makes scope-confusion bugs unwriteable.
AttributeDefinition.title: AttributeDefinition

Authority.description: An agency that issues credentials or administers obligations.
Authority.title: Authority

BusinessEntity.description: A legal entity. The company scope.

affiliation_group_id.description: Affiliate grouping, which size standards aggregate across.

company_peak_employment_prior_cy.description: Peak employment across the ENTIRE company in the prior calendar year. Deliberately named with a company scope, because size-based exemptions are company-wide while industry-based exemptions are per-site.

BusinessEntity.title: BusinessEntity

ChemicalHolding.description: A chemical held at a process. Data class is restricted.
ChemicalHolding.title: ChemicalHolding

ClassificationAssignment.description: A candidate or confirmed code for a subject. Candidates are presented ranked for human confirmation; only a confirmed assignment may be the code of record.

alternatives_shown.description: What the applicant was offered, not merely what they chose. Competent people disagree on the same description; an appeal needs the offered set.

ClassificationAssignment.title: ClassificationAssignment

CodeTranslation.description: The result of walking one or more correspondences. The hop path is retained so a translation can be audited rather than trusted.

is_composable.description: True only when every hop is an exactMatch. Close-match chains never auto-compose.

CodeTranslation.title: CodeTranslation

Concept.description: A single code within a scheme version. Identity is the triple (scheme, vintage, code) -- never a bare code.

id.description: Synthetic key. The natural key is (scheme, vintage, code).

Concept.title: Concept

apportionment_ratio.description: Local extension. XKOS 1.2 defines no such property.

ConfirmationState.description: Whether a classification has been affirmed by a person. Only a non-unconfirmed assignment may be referenced by a determination.
ConfirmationState.title: ConfirmationState

Correspondence.description: A published crosswalk between two scheme versions, as an addressable and versionable object rather than a lookup table.
Correspondence.title: Correspondence

Credential.description: A licence, certification, registration, or permit.

industry_code_vintage.description: Local extension supplying the vintage CTDL omits.

industry_codes.description: Adopted from CTDL, which types this as an untyped string with no vintage validation, so codes from different revisions are indistinguishable.

Credential.title: Credential

CredentialDependencyEdge.description: A derived, typed edge used for topological ordering. Cycles are a transcription error in the source law and fail CI; they are not a runtime condition to handle.
CredentialDependencyEdge.title: CredentialDependencyEdge

DataClass.description: Disclosure sensitivity, which governs storage and model egress.
DataClass.title: DataClass

Determination.description: A reproducible answer. Pinning the rule version, the law date, and a hash of the inputs is what lets the system answer "why did it say that in March".

classification_assignment.description: MUST reference an assignment whose confirmation_state is not `unconfirmed`. Enforced by a database CHECK constraint, not by application code.

evidence_tree.description: The predicate tree annotated with truth values and citations.

missing_attributes.description: What must be answered next when the result is indeterminate.

Determination.title: Determination

Establishment.description: A single physical site operated by a business entity.

jurisdiction_path.description: Ordered nation to place. A set, never a scalar.

Establishment.title: Establishment

Fact.description: An open-world fact carrying the long tail of attributes that do not warrant a typed column.
Fact.title: Fact

JurisdictionProfile.description: A jurisdiction expressed as an inclusion set with exceptions, because "everywhere except one state" is a common real pattern that a flat column cannot represent.
JurisdictionProfile.title: JurisdictionProfile

LegalSource.description: A retrieved, hashed, point-in-time snapshot of authoritative text. Every obligation traces to one of these.
LegalSource.title: LegalSource

ListSemantics.description: Whether a code list is exhaustive. The single most consequential distinction in the model: a hit on either kind proves inclusion, but only a closed list can prove exclusion.
ListSemantics.title: ListSemantics

MatchType.description: SKOS mapping relation between two concepts.
MatchType.title: MatchType

NodeType.description: Boolean structure of a requirement or predicate tree node.
NodeType.title: NodeType

non_waivable.description: Survives every exemption in its regime. A non-waivable obligation is surfaced even when the applicant is otherwise exempt.

Process.description: An activity unit beneath an establishment. Exists because chemical-process regimes attach codes and quantity thresholds below the site level, and forbid inheriting the site's primary code as a default.
Process.title: Process

ProductOffering.description: A product or service offered. A separate demand-based axis; not derivable from the supply-based industry classification.
ProductOffering.title: ProductOffering

ProvenanceRecord.description: What produced a surfaced item. No obligation is displayed without one.
ProvenanceRecord.title: ProvenanceRecord

Regime.description: A regulatory programme that generates obligations.
Regime.title: Regime

Requirement.description: A reified condition between a credential and what it demands. A table rather than a foreign key, because the edge carries jurisdiction, residency, experience, cost, and dates. Recursive: AND groups contain OR alternative sets contain further groups, which is what real licensing paths need.

target_predicate.description: A predicate from the rules DSL. This is the seam that unifies the regulatory and credential halves of the system into a single evaluator.

Requirement.title: Requirement

RevisionStatus.description: A concept's fate across scheme revisions. `reused` is the dangerous one: the same code string carrying a different concept in a later vintage.
RevisionStatus.title: RevisionStatus

RollupMethod.description: How a code at one scope is derived from codes at a narrower scope.
RollupMethod.title: RollupMethod

RollupRule.description: How a code at a wider scope derives from a narrower one, as data. Encoding this as rows is what lets one regime forbid the roll-up that another requires.
RollupRule.title: RollupRule

is_industry_scheme.description: False for code spaces that look like industry codes but are not, and must never be crosswalked as though they were.

SchemeVersion.description: A dated edition of a scheme. Vintage is part of concept identity.
SchemeVersion.title: SchemeVersion

ScopeUnit.description: The unit of analysis a fact, predicate, or obligation attaches to. Declared explicitly on every attribute and every predicate, because regulations key to different units and conflating them produces wrong determinations in both directions.
ScopeUnit.title: ScopeUnit

TruthValue.description: Kleene three-valued logic, with the unknown case split by what resolves it.
TruthValue.title: TruthValue
